I'm posting this review 15 years after the events, but I think my experience might be helpful to other owners.

At the time, my dog, a 5-year-old Golden Retriever named Topaze, was exhibiting significant behavioral problems, including occasional aggression in certain situations.

I consulted Dr. Dramard, who, based on my description, diagnosed hypothyroidism and told me that a test to confirm the diagnosis wasn't necessary. However, I had stated that I was prepared to pay for the test myself.

So, I followed the treatment for about two years, with regular adjustments, but without any noticeable or lasting improvement in my dog's behavior.

I finally had the confirmatory test done at a veterinary school. The results showed that Topaze did not have hypothyroidism.

I tried to inform Dr. Dramard, but despite leaving a voicemail, I never received a response.

I'm not saying that a misdiagnosis is impossible; my experience is simply that of a homeowner who, in hindsight, wishes the diagnosis had been confirmed before starting long-term treatment.

My advice to homeowners: when possible, don't hesitate to request a diagnostic confirmation, even if the examination is expensive. This can prevent unnecessary treatment and allow for a quicker search for the true cause of the problem.

We consulted Dr. Dramard for our dog, who was exhibiting aggression problems, particularly during encounters with other dogs and in certain everyday situations where he could quickly become agitated. The situation was becoming difficult to manage and a source of stress for us.

The follow-up took place over several consultations, which allowed us to take the time to analyze the context, the environment, and our habits. Dr. Dramard asked many questions and carefully observed our dog's behavior. The discussions were always professional, calm, and non-judgmental. The explanations were clear and helped us better understand the mechanisms behind these aggressive reactions.

The advice given was concrete and tailored to our situation (managing walks, anticipating difficult situations, adjusting our approach). It wasn't a miracle cure or an immediate solution, but gradually, by applying the recommendations, we observed a positive change in our dog's behavior and better management of risky situations.

This support has allowed us to regain confidence and approach daily life with greater peace of mind. I recommend Ms. Dramard to anyone facing behavioral problems in their dog and seeking serious and thoughtful guidance.

Dr. Dramard puts all her experience at the service of animals. She is attentive to their well-being. She diagnosed my little Shih Tzu, who was very stressed. She prescribed the appropriate treatment, which was effective. It needed some fine-tuning. She was very attentive to the evolution of her behavior during our monthly consultations, and after three months, the correct dosage was found. Since then, my little girl's behavior has literally changed; it seems she has regained her confidence.

Thank you so much, Valérie.
I will give you an update in three months, as you requested.

Thank you to Dr. Dramard for her professionalism and great empathy in handling complex cases.

It's a pleasure to work with her. Her extensive experience with hypothyroidism, unfortunately still very often underdiagnosed and poorly understood, can be the cause of significant behavioral problems and suffering for the animal.
Dr. Dramard manages to find the right balance for thyroid hormone dosages, which helps to resolve situations where owners and trainers are stuck. She is a great support. A big thank you for her help. I also thank her for the Hypolit chart, which is a fantastic and easy-to-use tool for both professionals and owners.

Ms. Dramard has been treating my dog ​​for his thyroid problems for almost five years. She has enabled him to live a nearly normal life. He is much more comfortable and emotionally balanced. I recommend Ms. Dramard wholeheartedly. Beyond her professional qualities, she is also a kind, attentive, and very compassionate person.

A fraud. As many comments have indicated, Dr. Drammard only offers one diagnosis: hyperthyroidism, even when blood tests contradict her diagnosis. She is convinced she has found the miracle cure, prescribes medications that are dangerous for dogs' health, and charges exorbitant fees. I spent several months paying €75 for 10-minute sessions where she offers absolutely no advice other than to continue the treatment, or even increase the dosage if the dog's behavior doesn't comply. She is neither a competent veterinarian nor a trustworthy behaviorist: Dr. Drammard is a quack (any veterinarian in Lyon will tell you the same, try it yourself). My vet told me that the veterinary board is closely examining her case following numerous complaints. If you care about your pet's health, do not consult this woman.

My dog ​​was seen by Dr. Dramard, who diagnosed him with hypothyroidism. He was put on Levothyroxine and, most importantly, cortisone for almost two years. This heavy treatment caused him to gain a lot of weight, and I was assured he would have to take it for life.

Fortunately, I eventually sought a second opinion from another veterinarian. She immediately alerted me: my dog ​​wasn't actually hypothyroid, and taking these medications unnecessarily could have caused him to have a heart attack.

Since I completely stopped this treatment, my dog ​​is doing much better: he has regained his energy, lost weight, and his overall health has clearly improved.

Looking back, I feel this diagnosis was made too hastily. And I'm very troubled to learn that many dogs systematically leave this clinic with the same diagnosis.

I strongly advise pet owners not to rely on just one opinion before agreeing to hormonal or cortisone-based treatment. In my case, it literally saved my dog's life.

My dog ​​has been seeing this vet for several years, and I'm absolutely delighted. She's incredibly professional, always attentive, and very responsive. If there's a problem, she's always there, even outside of scheduled appointments. She takes the time to explain things clearly, she's very patient and gives lots of helpful advice and tips, always with kindness. It's truly reassuring to be able to rely on someone like her. You can tell she loves animals and their owners, and that she's passionate about her work. I recommend her without hesitation!

I never leave negative reviews, but this is too serious not to raise the alarm. I agree with several comments already posted. Dr. Dramard only diagnoses hypothyroidism. She quickly observes the dog in her consultation room without even examining him and doesn't perform any tests, yet she makes the diagnosis. No differential diagnosis is carried out, even though this is one of the essential foundations of medicine...

Then, the vet sends you for blood tests, but be careful not to just any vet, or you might hear that her hypothyroidism diagnoses are given without any scientific evidence. Even if the blood test comes back normal, it means nothing, and she prescribes high doses of hormones for your dog.

Follow-up appointments are only via video call and are very expensive. Each time, you have to explain the dosages again... My dog's health has deteriorated significantly; he has become hysterical around food, has gained a lot of weight, and has started marking inside the house. Given the ineffectiveness of the prescribed hormones, Dr. Dramard advised me to give him anti-anxiety medication. I then consulted another veterinarian for a second opinion. We stopped everything and started from scratch with nutrition, natural supplements, and exercises tailored to my dog.

In short, a very bad experience for both my dog ​​and me. You can't mold a dog with hormones and other medications; each dog has its own personality and history that must be taken into account! Not to mention the long-term side effects of such medications, they shouldn't be taken lightly.

Despite this person's kindness, the diagnosis given to my dog ​​was completely wrong, and the prescribed treatment could have endangered him.

We consulted Valérie Dramard on the recommendation of our trainer because our dog, a border collie, was showing symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).

The first session wasn't a true analysis: we placed our dog in the center of the office, she observed him, called him, and watched his behavior with a toy. And that was it.

A blood test was performed. The results were generally normal, with a measurement "close to the limit."

Yet, the conclusion was that the OCD was probably linked to a hormonal problem, with a strong suspicion of hypothyroidism.

For several months, we gave our dog many pills:
-Fluoxetine
-Hydrocortisone
-Levothyroxine
-Euthyral

His condition didn't really improve. He became lethargic, barely moved, and lost all interest in everything. He was knocking less, but he also stopped eating and being active.

The follow-up appointments with Valérie Dramard became increasingly unprofessional. She insisted on video calls. When I went in person anyway, it was made clear that this wasn't preferred (except for the first appointment).

The consultations were very short (15 minutes) and very expensive (€60, or €240 per hour). At that price, you expect real professionalism, but that wasn't the case.

During those 15 minutes:

- We had to repeat the treatment given to our dog because she had forgotten it,

- And describe the progression of the symptoms, despite the daily delivery of a detailed chart.

In reality, 10 minutes were spent repeating information already provided.

Even worse, during follow-up appointments, she would ask us: "So, should we increase the dose or not? What do you want to do?"

We weren't doing our own shopping. It was her job to advise us, not the other way around. If a specialist asks their clients to choose the hormone dosage, that's very worrying.

We quickly realized that the appointments were scheduled without any preparation, which is unacceptable given the fees charged, which are well above average.

Finally, we consulted other professionals. At the veterinary school, our dog underwent a thorough behavioral analysis: 90 minutes of observation in various situations (throwing, toys, food, searching, commands, etc.).

Combined with the existing blood test results, the diagnosis was clear: our dog did not have hypothyroidism.

All medications were stopped because they were putting him at risk for no good reason.

Instead, behavioral recommendations were implemented. These allowed our dog to progress without sedating him.

Since then, we've been in contact with many people in the field. Valérie Dramard is well-known in Lyon, but unfortunately for the wrong reasons: hasty diagnoses, dangerous hormonal treatments, and questionable methodology.

We've heard several similar accounts.

I appreciate her as a person; she's pleasant and we had good communication. But my priority remains my dog's health. And based on our experience, it was clearly put at risk.

Dr. Dramard saved my 4-year-old Bernese Mountain Dog who was very ill. The illness was due to her thyroid. A true professional who knows animals and the subject very well. A thousand thanks again. Catherine Didierlaurent

After several trips to the emergency vet for our Pomeranian, barely a year old, who had developed alopecia after being neutered, and despite no veterinarian who had seen or treated our dog knowing what to do (he was supposedly fine), we …
I want to share my exceptional experience with Dr. Dramard, a veterinarian who proved to be a true expert in canine hypothyroidism. …
€180 for a video consultation, no results! Prescribed medication that had adverse effects on our dog! I do not recommend them!!!
I recommend Dr. Dramard for her welcoming manner and excellent care of my cat, who has been doing much better since starting treatment. Dr. Dramard is kind and attentive.

I am deeply disappointed with the service provided by this canine behaviorist. After entrusting my dog ​​to her care, she was diagnosed with hypoadrenocorticism and hyperthyroidism, based solely on a superficial blood test. …
